headline_marked: [[Senior Engineer's API]] Follows Rules for Predictable URLs
headline: Senior Engineer's API Follows Rules for Predictable URLs
summary: Learn to design REST APIs with predictable URLs, using plural nouns, IDs, and resource-based actions for better maintainability.
details: Most initial APIs present a simple list of URLs, often one for each button. A senior engineer's approach, however, involves a set of core rules that make every address predictable and guessable.

Key principles include using a plural noun followed by an ID (e.g., GET /posts/42 instead of GET /getPost?id=42), as the HTTP method already conveys the verb. IDs are preferred over names for resources (e.g., /users/7 instead of /users/jane_old) because an ID-based link remains stable even if the resource's name changes.

Nesting is kept to a single level for clarity, such as /posts/42/comments to list comments for a specific post. Individual comments can be accessed directly at /comments/99. Actions are treated as resources, like POST /posts/42/likes for liking a post, and the corresponding unlike action would be a DELETE request to the same endpoint.

Verbs are reserved for actions that don't naturally fit a noun, such as POST /posts/42:archive for an action that results in no stored resource. While servers can be scaled up to handle traffic growth, APIs are more challenging to change because installed applications will continue to call the old structure for years.
